newsitem.title: USA: U.S. drug companies beat estimates, shares rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. drug companies beat estimates, shares rally.

text.p: Pharmaceutical company shares rose Tuesday as three major U.S. drugmakers reported slightly better-than-forecast fourth quarter earnings, showing strong unit volume gains in new and established drugs.

"Earnings for the ethical drug companies are going back to levels seen at the start of the decade, except the quality of earnings is better," James Keeney, an analyst at Rodman & Renshaw said. "These are unit-volume driven gains, not driven by double-digit price increases."
Shares in most of the major U.S. drug companies were higher in afternoon trading Tuesday.
Merck and Co reported earnings of $0.87 per share in the fourth quarter, versus $0.70 per share a year ago.It topped the First Call analysts' mean estimate of $0.86.
Warner-Lambert Co fourth quarter earnings of $0.63 per share, compared to $0.45 the year earlier, also bested the First Call mean estimate of $0.62 per share.
American Home Products Corp beat First Call's analysts mean estimate of $0.78 per share with its fourth quarter earnings of $0.80 per share, up from $0.13 the year earlier.

"Merck did extremely well in the quarter," Jack Lamberton, an analyst at NatWest Securities, said. "They have had a history of beating consensus estimates and they did it again. The company had strong top-line growth and controlled expenses, which was a bit of a surprise."

Merck shares rose 2-5/8 to 87-1/8, Warner-Lambert shares were up 1-5/8 to 75-1/4, and American Home Products shares rose 7/8 to 60-5/8 in afternoon trading. Shares of Eli Lilly and Co, which reported earnings on Monday was up 3-5/8 to 84.
Bristol-Myers Squibb Co shares rose 3 to 121-1/8, while Pfizer Inc shares were up 1-3/8 to 87-1/8.
Merck said sales growth for the period was led by established products and new product introductions, and by growth from the Merck-Medco managed care business.

Keeney said earnings were helped by the fact that 55 percent of the quarter's pharmaceutical sales came form new pharmaceutical products launched since 1995. "There was also strong growth in established products," he said.
Merck said sales of Zocor, which aims to prevent heart attacks in people with high cholesterol and heart disease, grew 36 percent in the fourth quarter to $835 million.
In a statement, Warner-Lambert, which also beat analysts estimates, said it expected on average to post double-digit increases in sales and mid-teens growth in earnings through the end of the decade.
"At first glance, Warner's earnings were good, but it doesn't even matter much because the company is more of a 1997 or 1998 story," Steve Lasli, an analyst at Mehta and Isaly.
Warner-Lambert said in a statement its earnings growth projections were based partly on new pharmaceutical products being developed and introduced, including Lipitor, a cholesterol reducer, it said.
"Warner also benefited from favorable comparisons," Keeney said.
American Home Products earnings reflected growth of its hormone replacement therapies Premarin products, analysts said.

The company said its U.S. pharmaceutical sales increased 15 percent in the fourth quarter and 11 percent for the full year. But it said U.S. consumer health care sales fell six percent for the fourth quarter, and rose two percent in 1996. ((New York newsdesk 212-859-1707))
